stem: A hospital is considering reprocessing a device originally labeled for single use. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Some single-use devices may be reprocessed, but the reprocessor must meet applicable FDA requirements.
options.B: Every single-use device may be reprocessed without validation, labeling review, or regulatory oversight.
options.C: FDA prohibits reprocessing every device labeled for single use regardless of the device or validated process.
options.D: Hospital reprocessors are exempt from manufacturer-type FDA requirements for quality and safety.

rationale: FDA states that not all single-use devices are suitable for reprocessing, but some can be demonstrated safe and effective through validated reprocessing. Third-party and healthcare-facility reprocessors are regulated as manufacturers and must meet applicable requirements such as premarket, labeling, quality-system, and postmarket obligations. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize that selected single-use devices may be reprocessed only when applicable FDA requirements are met; healthcare-facility reprocessors are not exempt from manufacturer-type regulatory obligations.

audit_findings.source_authority: FDA primary medical-device guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: FDA Reprocessing Single-Use Medical Devices healthcare-facility guidance
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately preserves that some—but not all—SUDs may be reprocessed under applicable FDA requirements.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because validation and regulatory oversight are required where applicable.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because FDA does not categorically prohibit reprocessing every single-use device.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because healthcare-facility reprocessors are subject to applicable manufacturer-type requirements.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accurately reflects FDA's conditional reprocessing framework.
audit_findings.cueing: All options state regulatory propositions about the same practice.
